doc.title: Gerald Wilson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Black composers: Hale Smith, George Walker, Ulysses Kay
summary: Brown asks about Wilson's place among Black composers; Wilson discusses Hale Smith, George Walker and Ulysses Kay.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well I want to go – I want to turn back to – I know I mentioned Hale Smith, but you know – as a composer you can do that without – you know you can do that from home, but you seem to still be thriving as a composer. So I just wanted to talk about your relationship and/or place among African-American composers. Now when you mentioned William Grant Still, of course we all know him because of Afro-American Symphony, but there are other composers who are younger than you are, or maybe even your contemporaries. And the people I’m thinking of are George Walker, we mentioned Hale Smith…
George Walker, ooh, he’s so good.
…And there’s TJ Anderson, you know TJ Anderson? He’s at Duke University – TJ, TJ – yeah well he’s – that was his last position. And the other person is Ollie Wilson, do you know Ollie Wilson?
Yeah, ‘cause I was at Duke a couple years ago, yeah I did a concert with that band.
Yeah, TJ would have been there, ‘cause when Hale Smith died, TJ wrote a memorial.
Yeah, John – the guy’s name is John Brown. ‘Cause he’s head – like I said, “Your name is John Brown?” [laughs] Yeah well I was down there, yeah they were really nice, real nice.
And how about Hale Smith? Talk about…

Hale Smith – well Hale – I met him, you know I talked with – he liked my work, and I liked his work. He had done some work with Eric Dolphy, Eric Dolphy introduced me to Hale, Mr. Hale Smith. He just died, huh.
That’s so sad. He was nice, he was nice.
Yeah. And you mentioned George Walker, also.

George Walker, now I heard his music, man. That’s a black composer. They sure should have had him, because he really was in another world. He’s in another world, and um, I wish I had a chance to meet him. Is he still living?
I believe he is, because I used to see him at Rutgers, when I was at Rutgers, he was there. I’m thinking of another composer, how about Ulysses Kay?
Ulysses Kay? Yeah. Ulysses Kay, a very fine writer. I like him, yeah I like him. Now this record that I have now
